message.content: Improve the customer WEBMAIL composer + client UX in the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + React, customer portal under app/dashboard). Work on the current `main` (clean tree). Do NOT deploy/commit/db-push/build-in-place — I integrate centrally. ## Context / existing code (read these first) - `components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx` — the rich-text compose box (contentEditable editor with bold/italic/underline, font size, colour, lists, inline image paste). It already has a working SEND pipeline you MUST NOT break: `prepareComposedBody()` in `components/customer/mail/compose-html.ts` lifts base64 images → `cid:` refs and runs `safeHtml`, then sends via `lib/actions-mail.ts`. Preserve this end to end. - `components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx` — orchestrates the mail UI (folder rail + message list + reading pane + compose/reply). - `components/customer/mail/FolderRail.tsx` — the mailbox folder sidebar (Inbox/Starred/Sent/etc.). - `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` + `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the dashboard shell that wraps every customer page. ## What to build (5 items) 1. **Composer fixed to the VIEWPORT, not the document.** Today the compose/reply box sits in document flow and centers on the page, so on a long email/page the user must scroll to find it. Make it `position: fixed` and centered in the viewport (Gmail-style floating panel) so it's ALWAYS visible regardless of scroll. Give it a sensible max-height with its own internal scroll; never let it push page layout. 2. **Fixed/sticky mailbox sidebar.** `FolderRail` should stay put (sticky/fixed) while the reading pane scrolls a long email — folders always reachable. 3. **Recipient chips.** To and Cc become chip inputs: type an email, press **Enter** or comma → it becomes a removable chip; support MULTIPLE recipients; validate email shape (soft — allow paste of comma/space-separated lists that split into chips). The send payload must send all chip addresses (keep the existing payload shape `lib/actions-mail.ts` expects — check it). 4. **Resize images in the editor.** Images pasted/inserted into the contentEditable body can be resized — drag handles OR small/medium/large/full width presets on click. The chosen size must persist into the sent HTML (inline `width`/`style` on the ``), and survive `prepareComposedBody`/`safeHtml` (verify `safeHtml` keeps width/style on img, or carry it as an allowed attr — check `lib/mail/render.ts`). 5. **Minimize + keep alive across pages.** Add a minimize control that collapses the composer to a small docked bar (e.g. bottom-right); clicking restores it. CRUCIALLY the composer (and its in-progress draft) must SURVIVE navigating to other dashboard pages. Implement this by lifting compose state to a **dashboard-layout-level provider** (a `ComposeProvider` React context) that renders the composer via a portal at the shell root, exposing `openCompose()` / `openReply(message)` / `minimize()` / `close()`. Mail pages call the context to open; the provider keeps it mounted across route changes. A minimized composer stays docked on every page until sent or discarded. ## Architecture guidance - The provider likely mounts in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` (server component) via a small client wrapper, or inside `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (already `"use client"`). The composer moves OUT of the mail page into the provider/portal so it persists. `MailClient` triggers it through the context instead of rendering it inline. - Keep a single source of truth for the draft in the provider so minimize/restore/navigate never lose text, recipients, subject, or attachments. - Preserve the reply-quoting behaviour and the existing send action wiring. ## Platform rules (non-negotiable) - Preserve the send pipeline and its safety (client + server `safeHtml`, cid inline images). Don't regress sending. - `npx tsc --noEmit` must be clean for your files. Tests run via `npm test` (node:test). - Add tests that BITE for the pure/logic parts: recipient parsing/validation (email splitting on enter/comma, dedupe, invalid rejection), image-size persistence into HTML, and source tripwires (via `stripComments`/`stripCommentsAndStrings` from `test/_source-tools.ts`) proving the composer is rendered through the provider/portal (not inline) and the send still routes through `prepareComposedBody`. - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any minimize animation; keyboard-accessible (Esc minimizes or closes, focus management on open). - Do NOT run prisma/build/commit/deploy/systemctl. Report your file list + test count when done. ## Deliver Self-contained, typechecking code + tests. Final report: files created/changed, the exact wiring point (which file mounts the ComposeProvider), test count, and anything you changed in the send/safeHtml path (should be minimal — ideally only allowing img width/style if not already allowed). Report is data for me, not a user message.
